title: U.S. and Canada in a Big Trade Fight: No More Cheese or Motorcycles?
summary:
Imagine if your favorite cheese or motorcycle suddenly couldn't cross the border from Canada to the U.S. That's happening now! The U.S. says it will ban dairy products, most alcoholic drinks, and motorcycles from Canada. This is part of a big trade war between two countries that used to be best friends.

A trade war is when countries argue about money and taxes on things they buy and sell to each other. Canada was mad because the U.S. put extra taxes on some Canadian goods. So Canada said, "Fine, we'll put extra taxes on your stuff too!" They put taxes on $20 billion worth of U.S. things. That's a LOT of money—like buying 4 billion ice cream cones!

The U.S. president, Donald Trump, got even more upset. He said Canadian products can't be used in big U.S. government projects until Canada treats American products fairly.

Canada's leader, Mark Carney, said his country wants to be more independent. That means they don't want to rely on the U.S. so much. He said, "No country can hold us hostage." That's a strong way of saying they want to be their own boss.

This fight started because the U.S. thought Canada wasn't being fair to American dairy, alcohol, and car companies. Canada has special rules to protect its own dairy farmers.

Even though they're arguing, Canada still sends most of its stuff—over 70%—to the U.S. That's like if you gave most of your lunch to one friend every day. Now Canada wants to share with other friends too.

Carney says the fight will hurt a little now, but it will help Canada in the long run. He's going to Europe to talk about making new friends for trading. This is a big deal because the U.S. and Canada have been close allies for a long time. Let's see if they can make up!
why_it_matters: Trade fights can change what products are available and how much things cost, and they show that even countries need to cooperate.

keywords.explanation: When two countries fight by putting taxes on each other's goods instead of using soldiers.
To say that something is not allowed.
The line that separates two countries.
Countries that are friends and support each other.
Able to make your own choices and not depend on someone else.
Foods made from milk, like cheese and yogurt.

questions.question: What is happening because of the U.S.-Canada trade fight?
options: The U.S. is banning some products from Canada.
Canada is taking over the U.S. government.
The U.S. and Canada are going to war with soldiers.
Canada is closing its border to all visitors.
questions.correct_answer: The U.S. is banning some products from Canada.

questions.question: Which three kinds of Canadian products does the U.S. say it will ban?
options: cars, computers, and cheese
apples, lumber, and fish
dairy products, most alcoholic drinks, and motorcycles
toys, clothes, and ice cream cones
questions.correct_answer: dairy products, most alcoholic drinks, and motorcycles

questions.question: Why did Canada put extra taxes on $20 billion worth of U.S. things?
options: Because the U.S. first put extra taxes on some Canadian goods
Because Canada wanted more ice cream cones
Because Canada wants to buy the U.S. government
Because Canada wanted to stop all trade
questions.correct_answer: Because the U.S. first put extra taxes on some Canadian goods

questions.question: What did U.S. President Donald Trump say after Canada added the taxes?
options: Canada must give the U.S. free cheese.
Canadian products can't be used in big U.S. government projects until Canada treats American products fairly.
American companies must move to Canada.
Canada must put all its dairy farms up for sale.
questions.correct_answer: Canadian products can't be used in big U.S. government projects until Canada treats American products fairly.

questions.question: What did Canada's leader Mark Carney say about being independent?
options: We will never trade again.
No country can hold us hostage.
The U.S. should pay Canada money.
Canada wants to join the U.S.
questions.correct_answer: No country can hold us hostage.

questions.question: Where is Mark Carney going to talk about making new trading friends?
options: Mexico
Europe
China
Australia

background_read: Canada and the United States are neighbors that share the longest border between two countries in the world.
Most of Canada's trade goes to the U.S., so a trade fight between them affects lots of real products and jobs.
Donald Trump is the president of the U.S., and Mark Carney is the prime minister of Canada, so they are the leaders on each side of this fight.
Article_Structure: WHO: U.S. President Donald Trump, Canada's leader Mark Carney, and the governments of both countries.
WHAT: The U.S. plans to ban Canadian dairy products, most alcoholic drinks, and motorcycles, while Canada is adding taxes on U.S. goods.
WHERE: The fight is between the United States and Canada across their shared border.
WHY: The U.S. thinks Canada is treating American dairy, alcohol, and car companies unfairly, and Canada wants to be more independent.

perspectives.description: The U.S. says it is protecting American companies and needs Canada to treat them fairly.
Canada wants to keep its own dairy farmers safe and not be pushed into decisions by the U.S.
They may face fewer choices or higher prices while the two countries argue.
